item.title: The Shannon Airport Group Wins Two Green Awards
item.description: The Shannon Airport Group has won two awards at the Green Awards 2026. The airport group won in both the Green Public Sector Organisation of the Year and Green Large Organisation of the Year categories. The Green Awards celebrate excellence in sustainability across Ireland, and acknowledge organisations that are leading the way in environmental innovation, sustainable business practices and climate action. Advertisement This year’s Green Awards had over 300 entries, a new record for the awards.

item.title: Listowel Writers' Week preview includes presentation from former Scottish First Minister
item.description: Former Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon will be presenting a prestigious literature award in Listowel this summer. Listowel Writers' Week has released a preview into what lies ahead for this year's edition of the literary festival. Now in its 55th year, it is the country's oldest literary festival, with the first edition taking place in 1971. item.title: Kerry College running apprenticeship open evening at Monavalley Campus this evening
item.description: Kerry College is running an apprenticeship open evening at its Monavalley Campus (V92 PW50) from 5pm to 8pm today. It's part of the college's 2026 open week. It will include 20 minute information talks in the learner support area, and a ‘Try a Skill’ area. item.title: Councillors want no more money spend on plans for CCTV at dumping black spots if cameras are not hidden
item.description: Several local representatives have called on Kerry County Council (KCC) not to spend any more money installing CCTV at dumping black spots if the cameras are not hidden. The issue was discussed at the recent full council meeting after independent councillor Jackie Healy Rae requested an update on the rollout. item.title: Transport Minister would rather invest money in new transport lines than on train catering carts
item.description: The Transport Minister has said he would rather invest the money that could be spent on train catering carts on new transport lines. Iarnród Eireann signed a contract for catering services last year for the Belfast and Cork lines only, leaving remaining rail lines with no services since they were stopped during the pandemic. item.title: Kerry industrial school survivor welcomes removal of criminal records and says they now have closure
item.description: The removal of criminal records for people put into reform and industrial schools has been welcomed by survivors and their families. Maurice Patton O’Connell was one of four survivors of reform and industrial schools who undertook a 52-day hunger strike outside the Dáil last year, campaigning for improved supports. item.title: Irish Football Members Should Vote On Israel Matches
item.description: Irish football members should vote on a decision on whether or not to play Israel in the Nations League. A group representing players has called for the FAI to ask its general assembly for directions. FAI chief executive David Courell stated yesterday the matches will take place this autumn with one of them being played in Dublin. item.title: Listowel Community Hospital Seeking General Staff Nurse for Temporary Position
item.description: Listowel Community Hospital is currently inviting applications for a General Staff Nurse to fill a temporary position, which is available immediately. item.title: Plans for major redevelopment of Phoenix Cinema get go-ahead
item.description: Plans for a major redevelopment of the Phoenix Cinema in Dingle have been given the go-ahead by Kerry County Council. The historic cinema was bought in 2024 by visual artist Yvonne McGuinness, and her husband, Oscar-winning actor Cillian Murphy. The team behind the redevelopment held several public meetings to outline their vision for the redevelopment, prior to seeking planning permission. item.title: Paediatric dermatology services close at UHK due to staffing shortages
item.description: Staffing shortages have led to the closure of paediatric dermatology services at University Hospital Kerry (UHK). HSE South West has confirmed that demand for dermatology services is now greater than the available resources. As a result, GPs in Kerry have been advised to refer children to specialist skin consultants in Dublin.
